events.title: WINTER PROVISIONS ARE CHECKED AS THE COLD CONTINUES
events.body: The stewards make another inspection of the grain, fodder, and preserved provisions remaining at the principal holding and the outlying estates. Nothing suggests an immediate shortage, but the stores are being drawn down steadily enough that careless distribution could create problems before winter ends. Valerius orders the keepers to maintain the established reserves and to report unusual demands before releasing additional quantities. Workers therefore begin shifting some supplies between the holdings where they are most needed. The arrangement remains the same system established during the preceding months rather than a new institution. For the estate, the immediate concern is simply to reach the opening of the agricultural season without allowing one holding to exhaust what another still possesses.

events.title: THE RAID INQUIRY CONTINUES THROUGH PRIVATE CORRESPONDENCE
events.body: A further communication connected with Quintus Caecilius Metellus Celer reaches Valerius concerning the account of the earlier raid. The questions concern the order in which several statements were received and the circumstances surrounding the merchant testimony already discussed in January. Valerius has the relevant correspondence brought together and answers from the information already preserved at the estate. Aulus Vettius remains part of the chain through which some of the material has passed, but the new communication does not establish any additional accusation against him. The exchange keeps the inquiry active without turning it into a public confrontation. For Valerius, the immediate result is a clearer understanding of which parts of the account still require explanation.

events.title: MERCHANTS PREPARE THE LAKE-PORT FOR THE FIRST SPRING MOVEMENT
events.body: The merchants who began arranging the next lake-port cycle in January now move from discussion toward practical preparation. Space is cleared in the existing warehouses, packing areas are inspected, and arrangements are made for weighing and receiving cargo when transport conditions improve. The work does not yet constitute a major new shipment, and no new harbor construction begins. Estate administrators compare the expected movement with the storage space already available. The merchants are therefore preparing to use the commercial facilities that already exist rather than expanding them. The lake-port is beginning to shift from winter inactivity toward the first traffic of the coming season.

events.title: SEVERAL SMALLHOLDERS JOIN THE BOUNDARY PETITION
events.body: The boundary complaint brought to Valerius during the January readings returns in a more substantial form when several neighboring smallholders appear together. They describe the disputed path and the points at which their recollections and older property descriptions differ. Valerius listens to the competing accounts and asks that the relevant descriptions and local testimony be assembled before any conclusion is reached. No judgment is issued during the gathering, and neither side is declared to have won the dispute. The petition nevertheless becomes more consequential because several households now have an interest in its resolution. What began as a request from one farmer has become a local matter requiring careful examination.

events.title: MARCELLUS'S CORRESPONDENCE BRINGS NEW QUESTIONS TO THE LIBRARY
events.body: A new communication associated with Marcus Claudius Marcellus reaches Valerius after the questions circulated from the winter readings. Marcellus asks about several passages discussed by the readers and is particularly interested in preserving the different interpretations rather than receiving a single polished answer. Valerius's scribes copy the questions and place them with the material already being discussed at the estate. Several local readers are invited to give their own responses before Valerius replies. The exchange remains scholarly and personal, with no formal appointment or political office arising from it. The library's correspondence nevertheless continues to reach beyond the immediate community.

events.title: THE FIRST FIELD WORK OF THE SEASON BEGINS
events.body: With conditions beginning to permit outdoor work, crews start clearing and preparing the fields identified during the earlier winter inspections. The first attention goes to areas where clearing and minor repairs must be completed before the ordinary planting work can begin. Stewards organize the labor around the existing holdings and keep track of the work still required before the agricultural season is fully underway. Nearby smallholders begin similar preparations on their own land. No new property changes hands, and the work does not expand Valerius's holdings. It marks instead the first visible transition from winter preservation toward the productive work of the coming season.

events.title: WINTER ADMINISTRATION GIVES WAY TO THE SPRING AGENDA
events.body: By the end of February the separate matters occupying the estate during winter have begun to converge into the preparations for spring. The remaining provisions, the unresolved boundary petition, the continuing raid correspondence, the lake-port arrangements, and the first field work all require attention as the weather improves. Valerius instructs his stewards and scribes to keep the relevant papers together so that decisions made in one matter can be compared with information arising in another. The estate therefore enters March with several unfinished affairs rather than a single dominant undertaking. None of them has yet produced a decisive change in Valerius's position. Their continued development, however, gives the opening weeks of spring several active threads from which further events can arise.
